# TCR AI-raters pilot

**[Open the live dashboard](https://nickson-quak.github.io/tcr-ai-raters-pilot/)**

Explore how three AI judges apply Transparency, Consistency, Refinement, and Overall to multi-turn conversations.

- [Model profiles](https://nickson-quak.github.io/tcr-ai-raters-pilot/#view=profiles): recurring associations, tentative judging tendencies, and linked evidence.
- [Study overview](https://nickson-quak.github.io/tcr-ai-raters-pilot/): agreement and native-field coverage.
- [Ratings explorer](https://nickson-quak.github.io/tcr-ai-raters-pilot/trace_casebook.html): displayed conversations, verdicts, and recorded native fields.
- [Methods](https://nickson-quak.github.io/tcr-ai-raters-pilot/#view=methods): denominators, primary observations, and limitations.
- Downloads: [numerical report](trace_results.json), [Markdown report](trace_results.md), and [profile analysis](profile_analysis.json).

The saved study contains 60 pairs and 1440 valid judgments, covering every configured judge, dimension, and both display orders. The earlier and fresh studies use the same pairs; the fresh judgments preserve native reasoning fields.

Agreement does not establish accuracy. Model profiles are task-specific observations, not innate personality. Curated examples are exploratory; native text is not a verified account of the decision process.

Public excerpts have identifying path segments and private network addresses redacted; ratings and statistics use the original frozen inputs.

Conversation excerpts come from [WildChat-1M (AllenAI)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/WildChat-1M), available under the [ODC Attribution License 1.0](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/by/1-0/).

See [data attribution and provenance](ATTRIBUTION.md). The site contains saved public research excerpts and performs no inference. Search-engine indexing is discouraged; the published files are publicly accessible.
